correctness.rationale: The actual vertex rank orbits O_k have sums S_k and squared norms Q_k, so every coordinate-permutation-invariant unique minimum ball center equals t 1_m. The strict convex radius objective is max_k(mt^2+Q_k-2tS_k). Adjacent differences (n-k)(n-k-2t) make exactly one rank or adjacent pair active on intervals I_k. Clipping the stationary S_k/m to each active interval yields exact global candidates and contact ranks. Uniform orbit barycenters and their convex mixing give a supporting distribution centered at t*1_m, providing the global certificate against non-symmetric competitor centers. Independently enumerated 121 rational (m,n) small cases and verified rank ties, subgradient, and m>n(n+1) threshold. Hausdorff cube convergence proves fixed-m n->infinity, not extrapolation from tests.
